goal: Make the post-merge WeChat preview refresh a repository-owned, cross-machine Harness closure action instead of a conversation-local habit.
userValue: After a WeChat frontend change is accepted and merged, developers can immediately preview the latest main build without accidentally opening stale dist output, even in a new session or on another configured computer.
nonGoals: Do not replace pre-merge candidate preview, CI or explicit user acceptance.
Do not install WeChat DevTools, enable its service port, accept agreements or modify credentials.
Do not upload a mini program, create preview QR codes or change product runtime behavior.
Do not change API, PostgreSQL, deployment, timer or production configuration.

mustChange: A repository script and npm command that build, verify and open the active apps/mini-taro project.
Harness and AGENTS user-acceptance closure sequences.
Cross-machine DevTools CLI discovery and explicit manual handoff.
Harness version declarations, current project state and owner-map characterization.
mustNotChange: The active 14-route mini-program source or generated package semantics.
Pre-merge manual acceptance and candidate preview requirements.
Backend, API, database, deployment, timer and production state.
evidenceRequired: Failing-then-passing refresh command tests covering build failure, output verification, macOS override, Windows discovery, CLI open and manual fallback.
Harness/current-truth/owner-map tests for the v0.6.4 closure sequence.
Harness profile on the complete task release packet.
Local CR and diff whitespace check.

engineeringHealth.reason: The command is a bounded Node built-in wrapper around the existing safe build and official DevTools CLI; dependency injection keeps platform discovery and error paths testable without launching tools during tests.

acceptanceEvidence: node --test tests/refresh-weapp-preview.test.js tests/project-harness.test.js tests/verify-project.test.js tests/project-state.test.js tests/project-owner-map.test.js tests/backend-owner-map.test.js
npm run refresh:weapp on latest main after merge

decisionLog.decision: After confirming the latest main preview flow worked, the user approved making the action persist across Codex sessions and computers through repository-owned rules and tooling.
